definitions.explanation: Internet slang for someone who has a satisfying offline life, including romantic relationships, active social life, and enjoyable activities. Originally used by online communities to describe people who don't spend all their time on the internet.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}はリア{充|じゅう}だから{週末|しゅうまつ}はいつも{予定|よてい}がある。
examples.english: That person has a fulfilling social life, so they always have plans on weekends.

examples.japanese: SNSでリア{充|じゅう}アピールするのは{疲|つか}れる。
examples.english: It's tiring to show off a fulfilling life on social media.

examples.japanese: 「リア{充|じゅう}{爆発|ばくはつ}しろ」はネットで{使|つか}われる{冗談|じょうだん}だ。
examples.english: "Riajuu bakuhatsu shiro" (explode, normies!) is a joke used online.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: Abbreviation of リアル{充実|じゅうじつ} (real life fulfillment). The term originated in Japanese internet culture, particularly among users of 2channel (now 5channel) in the late 2000s.

REGISTER: Casual/Slang
Primarily used among young people and in online contexts. Not appropriate for formal settings.

USAGE NOTES:
・Often used with self-deprecating humor by those who feel they aren't リア{充|じゅう}
・The phrase 「リア{充|じゅう}{爆発|ばくはつ}しろ」 (explode, people with lives!) is a common humorous complaint
・Can imply envy or mild resentment when used about others
・リア{充|じゅう}アピール means showing off one's fulfilling life (often on social media)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・リア{充|じゅう}アピール (showing off one's social life)
・リア{充|じゅう}{爆発|ばくはつ}しろ (explode, normies - humorous)
・リア{充|じゅう}じゃない (not having a fulfilling life)

CONTRAST:
・リア{充|じゅう}: has fulfilling offline life
・{非|ひ}リア{充|じゅう}/{非|ひ}リア: lacks fulfilling offline life (opposite)
